title: Eleven Yards of Movement
subtitle: 山川山地 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 山川山地（自然生态·山川与地形）
meta: 主题语境：山川山地（自然生态·山川与地形）　|　核心词汇：bend　|　正文 348 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bend 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 my grandfather walked to ① a bend in the river and stood there for nine minutes, and my grandmother said the standing was the whole of the walk. The ② bend, meaning the curve and not the water, had moved eleven yards since 1946 and was still called by the same name; a bend, he said, is the only piece of a river that stays where it is by moving.

Every ③ bend on that road was known by a different family, and the ④ bend by the willows, meaning the one where the cart went over in March and not either of those, was the only one anybody slowed down for. A bend, my mother said, is nine parts hedge and one part knowing what is coming; my grandfather said the hedge is the part that hides it.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ bend was the whole of the pipe, meaning the elbow and not the curve. The ⑥ bend, meaning the joint and not any of that, is the only part of a system that nobody plans and everybody blames; a bend, he said, is either a curve in a river or the only word that means both a turn and a joint. She said the joint is the part that leaks.

By 1968 the ⑦ bend had become a line on a survey, and the survey had become an argument about who owned the bank. The ⑧ bend of the whole thing, my grandfather wrote in April, was eleven yards of movement and nine minutes of standing; a bend, he said, is either the curve by the willows or the reason you learned to slow down. He said the slowing was the part that saved everybody.

The ⑨ bend I remember is the one by the willows, which was straightened in 1971 and is still described as dangerous. A ⑩ bend, my grandmother said in 1973, is the only thing that improves by being removed; every bend, she said, is a joint that has agreed to look like a curve. She said the joint was always the problem.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 河弯（指那个弯道，与河水相对）
C. 固定搭配：walk to a bend 走到一个河弯／弯道处
D. n. 弯道（指那条路上每一个）
E. n. 弯道（指柳树旁那一个）
F. n. 弯头；弯管接头（指管子的那个弯头）
G. n. 弯头（抽象：那种接头）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The bend, meaning the curve and not the water
bend was the whole of the pipe
the bend had become a line on a survey
The bend of the whole thing
A bend, my grandmother said in 1973

answers.why: walk to a bend 意为“走到一个河弯／弯道处”，1953 年祖父走到河的一个弯处，站了九分钟。
bend 意为“河弯”，指那个弯道而不是河水，它自 1946 年以来挪了十一码，却仍叫同一个名字。
bend 指那条路上每一个弯道，每一个都由不同人家命名。
bend 指柳树旁那一个弯道（三月翻车那一个），是唯一有人会减速的。
bend 意为“弯头、弯管接头”，指管子那个弯头，父亲说 bend 就是那根管子的全部。
bend 为抽象用法，指那种接头，是一套系统里没人规划、却人人归咎的部分。
bend 意为“弯道”，到 1968 年这个 bend 成了测量图上的一条线。
bend 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，祖父四月写道，整件事权衡下来是十一码的移动和九分钟的站立。
bend 意为“弯道”，我记得的是柳树旁那一个，1971 年被取直，至今仍被说成危险。
bend 为抽象总称，祖母说弯道是唯一会因为被取直而变好的东西。

父亲说 bend 就是那根管子的全部，指的是弯头而不是那个弯道。（bend）
